audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[1], whys[4] and mid all say Infinite Duress pins him 'through' Abyssal Dive. The page also credits a 'passive stun', a 'grey-health passive shield' and a 'self-peel devour'.
audit.why: Abyssal Dive knocks up, and a knockup cancels Warwick's channelled ult — the interaction runs the other way. The stun is delivered by Tongue Lash once An Acquired Taste reaches three stacks, the grey-health shield is Thick Skin (E, 3s), and Devour is his ultimate, used on an ally to pull them out of danger.
audit.corrected: Ult only after Abyssal Dive (21s at rank 1) is spent and his stacks are fresh; each effect reattributed to the ability that actually produces it.
sources: Tahm Kench kit W/E/R/P/Q text and cooldowns

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[2], whys[3] and whys[4] all say 'favours you' while win[2] said Tahm Kench and win[3]/win[4] said Skill — the page rendered two answers per row.
audit.why: The packet chart matches the prose and the 53.77% win rate: Warwick owns 1 and 3-6, level 2 and first item are even, and the two-item stage is Kench's as his HP and Thick Skin scale.
audit.corrected: Warwick, Skill, Warwick, Warwick, Warwick, Skill, Tahm Kench — paired across both layers with ratings raised on the Warwick rows.

audit.whatIsWrong: The first-item spike credited 'passive grey-health regen' for his sticky trades.
audit.why: Thick Skin converts stored damage into a shield on a 3s cooldown — that recurring shield, not a passive regen, is what makes him hard to burst once he has HP items.
audit.corrected: Thick Skin named with its 3s cooldown in the first-item spike.
sources: Tahm Kench kit E text and cd 3

edits.before: Level 6 favours you: R Infinite Duress pins him through W Abyssal Dive for a burst window.
edits.after: Level 6 favours you: ult only after Abyssal Dive; its knockup cancels your channel.

edits.before: 2+ items favour Tahm Kench: mass HP, self-peel devour, and passive stun outscale your DPS.
edits.after: 2+ items favour Tahm Kench: mass HP, Thick Skin, and Devour peel outscale you.

edits.before: R Infinite Duress pins him so he can't W Abyssal Dive out, but respect his W self-peel and grey-health passive shield — burst him before three Q stacks proc his passive stun.
edits.after: Abyssal Dive's knockup and a three-stack Tongue Lash stun both cancel Infinite Duress mid-channel — ult only once his W (21s at rank 1) is spent and your stacks are clean.

edits.before: Kench builds HP and his passive grey-health regen makes trades sticky; the lane sits at Skill as his tankiness and self-sustain start eating your DPS.
edits.after: Kench builds HP and Thick Skin (E) turns stored damage into a shield every 3s; the lane sits at Skill as his self-sustain starts eating your DPS.

edits.before: Late Tahm Kench is a mountain of HP with W devour peel, grey-health shielding, and a passive stun — your single-target damage can't kill him and he saves allies from your R.
edits.after: Late Tahm Kench is a mountain of HP with Thick Skin (E) shielding and a three-stack stun, and Devour (R) pulls an ally straight out of your suppression — bring anti-heal.

edits.before: Levels 3-6 are yours. Blood Hunt speed keeps you glued to him, Q sustain beats his Tongue Lash chip, and R at 6 pins him through W Abyssal Dive — just burst before his passive stacks to three and stuns you.
edits.after: Levels 3-6 are yours. Blood Hunt speed keeps you glued to him and Q sustain beats his Tongue Lash chip — but at 6 hold the ult until Abyssal Dive is spent, because its knockup cancels the channel.

edits.before: Use W Abyssal Dive to escape or peel with self-devour
edits.after: Use Abyssal Dive to escape, Devour to save an ally

edits.before: His escape + shield. R when down. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: His escape and knockup, 21s at rank 1 — ult only once it is spent.

notes: Three effects were attributed to the wrong abilities: the stun is Tongue Lash at three An Acquired Taste stacks (not 'the passive stun'), the grey-health shield is Thick Skin (E, 3s), and Devour is the ultimate used on an ally — there is no self-devour in Riot's text. The reversed interaction is the important one: Abyssal Dive's knockup cancels Infinite Duress rather than being pinned by it, which the tahmkench__warwick mirror already teaches from its side. Chart set to the packet chart because the why-lines already described it that way.
